title: GPU commitment guidance and risk log - customer workshop notes
body:
Context:
Quick capture from a 90-minute workshop with Customer: Nautilus Health (alpha POC). Goal: get them to a defensible committed GPU recommendation and enumerate the operational risks we need to mitigate in the Dedicated proposal.

High-level ask from customer:
- 99th percentile latency target: 220ms for chat flows (seq len 2048 on average)
- Concurrent QPS: 180 steady-state, with 4x daily peak spikes for marketing-driven campaigns
- Cost sensitivity: want to keep committed spend under $45k/month equivalent for first 6 months
- Data isolation required (PHI-ish), so Private/Dedicated preferred over hosted.

Notes / impressions from session:
- Customer emphasizes predictability over lowest unit cost. They are worried about burst overages and want clear fallback policies.
- Team has limited MLOps bandwidth; prefer our managed autoscale and warm pools rather than building custom tooling.
- Their traffic is bursty and driven by two predictable events (report generation at 03:00 UTC and marketing email sends).
- They do ~25% of queries that require longer completions (multi-step summaries), increasing average token output by ~2.6x on those requests.

Quick sizing heuristics we used in workshop (rules of thumb):
- Baseline single GPU throughput for the selected model family (redwood-rlm-13B-quant) = ~220 tokens/sec for generation-only flows at seq_len 2048, beam=1, kv-cache warm.
- Average tokens per request (customer): 380 tokens (prompt 140 + generation 240) -> per-request CPU/GPU time approx = 380 / 220 = 1.73s per concurrent request equivalent.
- Equivalent steady-state concurrency = QPS * latency_seconds -> 180 * 1.73 ≈ 311 GPU-concurrency units.
- Empirical consolidation factor for multi-tenant GPU (continuous batching) = 1.8–2.1 (assume 1.9 for planning). So required raw concurrency slots ≈ 311 / 1.9 ≈ 164.
- Map slots -> GPUs: typical GPU supports ~16 slots for this model at target latency (observed from internal perf baseline) -> GPUs_needed ≈ 164 / 16 ≈ 10.25 -> round to 11 GPUs.

Shortfall and burst strategy:
- Peak multiplier 4x -> brief bursts to ~720 QPS. That maps to GPUs_needed_peak ≈ 44 (using same math). Committing 44 GPUs is cost-prohibitive.
- Strategy proposed: commit 11 GPUs (steady) + burst buffer (pre-warmed volatile pool) and fallback model variants for high-concurrency windows.
- Suggested burst plan: 11 committed + 12 warm standby (pay slightly higher for burst on reserved cluster) + autoscale up to 44 using ephemeral cloud instances (no commitment). Warm standby configured to keep KV caches warm for top 5 customer routes only.

Cost estimate (back-of-envelope monthly):
- Committed 11x A100-equivalent monthly cost (on Redwood Dedicated pricing tiers + infra overhead + licensing) ≈ $32,500/month.
- Warm standby 12x (hot-swap pre-warm) incremental ≈ $6,600/month.
- Expected ephemeral autoscale usage (peaks, assumed 20 hours total across month at up to +33 GPUs) ≈ $4,200 amortized.
- Total ≈ $43,300/month (fits their $45k target with a small buffer).
- Sensitivity: If average tokens/request increases by 20% -> GPUs_needed increases ~20% -> committed cost would exceed $45k. Call this a primary risk.

Operational risk log (prioritized):
1) Traffic misprediction (undercommitting) -> user-facing latency or rejected requests. Mitigations: progressively increasing canary ramp (start 6 committed -> 11 -> 14), burst guards (queueing + graceful degrade to shorter completions), and conservative warm-standby for top routes. Owner: Solutions Eng, ETA: immediate.
2) Token inflation risk (customer changes prompts or enables longer outputs) -> capacity blowout. Mitigations: set SLA-bound prompt length caps, server-side quota enforcement, automated alerts on tokens-per-minute. Owner: Customer success + Solutions Eng.
3) Cold-cache bursts for rarely used routes -> latency spikes. Mitigation: selective KV pre-warm (top N routes), route-specific prewarm schedule, cache warming via synthetic traffic during known campaign windows. Owner: DevOps.
4) Billing disputes on burst usage -> unexpected overages. Mitigation: guaranteed burst budgets with hard caps, daily usage exports to customer, weekly sync. Owner: Account Exec.
5) Model degradation after quantization or variant fallback -> quality regressions. Mitigation: pre-release quality tests, baseline prompts to measure regression, automatic fallback to hosted model if regression detected. Owner: Applied ML + Product.

Decision tree for commitment size (playback to customer):
- If legal/finance requires <= $45k/month: commit to 11 GPUs with warm-standby 12 and autoscale cap 44 via ephemeral instances. Add hard burst cap policy and weekly review.
- If they can accept $60k/month: commit to 18 GPUs steady (reduces autoscale pressure and improves 99th latency headroom).
- If they want zero surprises and can sign 12-month term: evaluate a hybrid reserved discount -> 22 GPUs with deeper discounts.

Workshop action items (owner, due):
- Create formal Dedicated proposal doc with line-item pricing and runbook (Owner: Amina) Due: 2025-11-14. Linked Jira: JIRA-SOLENG-1567.
- Build small synthetic workload generator that matches their burst pattern for a soak test (Owner: Ethan) Due: 2025-11-07.
- Add route-level prewarm config to staging and run a 48h warm-cache experiment on 11+12 topology (Owner: Marisol) Due: 2025-11-20.
- Define token-metering alert thresholds and a billing visibility dashboard for customer (Owner: Platform Eng contact: Jonah) Due: 2025-11-12.

Open questions to resolve in follow-ups:
- Confirm expected token distribution after marketing campaigns (customer to share sample trace).
- Clarify tolerance for degraded completions (shortened summaries) during bursts.
- Legal: confirm acceptable overage billing cadence and invoice reconciliation window.

Appendix (short heuristics cheatsheet copied to email to customer):
- Quick GPU count = ceil( (QPS * avg_tokens / throughput_tokens_per_sec) / consolidation_factor / slots_per_gpu )
- Throughput_tokens_per_sec = measured for model at expected seq_len and batch mode (we measure this during proposal).
- Consolidation_factor: 1.6–2.2 depending on request shape and latency target. Use conservative 1.9 for first pass.

Notes to self (informal):
- Customer nervous about warm standby costs — highlight that warm standby is narrowly scoped to critical routes to keep price palatable.
- For final proposal, include 3 scenario tables: conservative, baseline (recommended), optimistic.
- Need to run cost sensitivity matrix: GPUs x avg_tokens x consolidation to show breakpoints.

References and links mentioned in discussion:
- Slack thread: #cust-nautilus-poc (pinned messages)
- Confluence: /spaces/PLAT/pages/8423/dedicated-commitment-guidelines
- Jira ticket: JIRA-SOLENG-1567 (proposal + signoff)
- Infra PR for autoscale caps: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/421

- 2025-11-05: added cost calc and risk list (Ethan)
